title: Microbatch sculpting: run-length clustering + pad-elision scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current bucket-based microbatching groups by coarse sequence-length ranges which leaves significant wasted padding for skewed workloads (chatty short requests mixed with occasional long prefill). This increases per-token cost and bumps p95 latency during prefill spikes. Goal: implement a 'microbatch sculpting' scheduler that performs run-length clustering and pad-elision at the microbatch level, integrating kernel selection hints to prefer low-overhead kernels for flattened batches and defer/shape prefill vs decode to hit latency SLOs. The feature should be toggleable per-customer and safe for rollout with fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end integration that reduces median padding tokens per GPU batch by >= 35% on mixed-length production traces.
2) p95 end-to-end latency for chat workloads does not regress by more than 5% under normal load; improves during prefill-heavy bursts.
3) No correctness regressions: outputs identical when pad-elision disabled; numerical differences within tolerances when using quantized kernels.
4) Feature gated, metrics surfaced in Console: pad tokens saved, effective batch size, kernel selection distribution.
5) Rollout capability with canary and automatic fallback to legacy bucketing on kernel incompatibility or SLO violations.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: offline prototype - run-length clustering script to produce microbatch groupings and simulate pad savings. Phase 2: runtime scheduler - implement 'sculpt' stage in request router that can reshape microbatches before enqueue with three actions: 1) coalesce similar run-lengths, 2) apply pad-elision by sending prefix KV-only metadata and masked input, 3) attach kernel-hint tags for backend. Phase 3: backend changes - accept masked microbatches and adapt kernel selection to prefer streamed-attention kernels when pad ratio low. Phase 4: experiments + canary rollout. Phase 5: telemetry and Console panels.
Key engineering notes: keep memory accounting conservative, maintain KV cache alignment, provide explicit fallbacks if downstream allocator/kernel rejects sculpted batch.
experiments_and_results: Experiment 2026-02-17: Offline run-length clustering on 7 days of prod trace (mixed chat + long generative). Result: avg padding tokens per batch reduced from 48 to 29 (39% reduction).

Experiment 2026-02-23: Microbench prefill/decode interleaving simulation. Shaping prefill to smaller microbatches during burst reduced p95 prefill latency by 22% at cost of 6% throughput loss for decodes. Good trade for SLO-sensitive customers.

Experiment 2026-03-02: Kernel hinting A/B on a staging fleet. When sculpted batches used 'stream-attn-lite' kernel, end-to-end token throughput increased 12% and CPU offload decreased 18%. One model variant with long kv density showed minor (1.5%) token quality delta under int8 kernel; flagged as acceptable by research.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-02-19: Use run-length clustering (k-means on sequence length with k adaptive to queue depth) instead of fixed-width bucketing to better match live distributions.
Decision 2026-02-25: Implement pad-elision via an explicit mask + compacted buffer representation; avoid in-place trimming to preserve alignment for KV cache lookup.
Trade-off: Aggressive sculpting reduces padding but can increase scheduling jitter. We will add a jitter budget and conservative fallback threshold tied to p95 observability.
Kernel selection policy: add 'PAD_RATIO' hint to kernel selector; prefer 'stream-attn' family when pad_ratio < 0.2 and sequence lengths are homogeneous (stddev < 16 tokens).
timeline: Week 1: prototype and offline sims. Week 2-3: runtime integration + unit tests. Week 4: staging canary with 5% traffic. Week 5: widen canary and add console metrics. Week 6: gradual rollout to 50% for P1 customers.
followups: Add per-customer sculpt policy UI in Console for Dedicated/Private customers.
Experiment with hybrid sculpting that folds very short decode requests into prefill tails when safe to reduce scheduling overhead.
Evaluate savings with structured sparsity kernels once available.
blockers: Need kernel team review and approval for new kernel hint semantics (meeting scheduled 2026-03-12).
GPU allocator changes required to accept compacted masked buffers (allocator RFC in review).
